title: Cuecraft: Prompt Variant Assembler & Failure Triage
content:
Intent: an informal working space for assembling small combinatorial sets of prompt variants (cue + scaffold + exemplar ordering) and tracking the recurring failure modes that show up across customers and internal tests. This is my personal scratchpad—notes to self, quick ideas, and triage hooks.

High-level goals:
- Build a compact combinator for creating 4–10-shot variants with controlled differences (role framing, instruction specificity, example ordering).
- Rapidly label failure classes and link to minimal repro prompts.
- Capture heuristics that map observed failure -> quick mitigation (e.g., add negative exemplar, tighten output schema, increase step-by-step signal).

Why this is different:
- Not a canonical playbook. Focused on small, incremental assemblies that are cheap to test on hosted model endpoints. Keeps tests tight (<= 512 tokens) to isolate prompt effects.

Notes / To-dos (quick):
- [ ] Implement small generator that emits permutations of: cue-template, few-shot set, ask-style (direct vs open), output constraint lines. (Ethan: prototype script?)
- [ ] Prioritize triage cases from CS backlog (see JIRA PRJ-2217) and add 6 canonical repros.
- [x] Dumped a first sweep of 40 variants for FAQ summarization task (see GH PR).

Quick definitions I use here:
- Cue-template: the opening framing sentence that orients role and goal ("You are an expert product summarizer...").
- Few-shot set: 1–8 exemplar pairs (input -> desired output) used to anchor style and structure.
- Scaffold: step-by-step or chain-of-thought hints, explicit markers like "Step 1/3".
- Negative exemplar: example of incorrect format or hallucination to discourage pattern.

Minimal repros (live examples to copy/paste):
1) Summarization (FAQ style) — brittle to list compression.
Cue: "You are an editor who compresses customer questions into 1-line FAQ bullets, preserving intent"
Examples (2-shot):
- Q: "How do I reset password if SSO fails?" -> A: "User can reset via Settings > Security; SSO flow unaffected."
- Q: "Does the app store data in EU?" -> A: "Data residency: EU data stored in eu-1 region unless customer opts out."
Prompt ask: "Compress into a one-line FAQ"
Observed failure: model invents steps ("navigate to Admin > Reset") — adding a negative exemplar that shows hallucinated step-level instruction reduces this.
Mitigation tried: add negative exemplar + short directive "Do not invent UI paths." -> reduce hallucination in 5/8 variants.

2) Rerank justification — degenerates to tautologies.
Cue: "You are a ranking assistant; provide a concise reason why candidate A > B."
Few-shot: 3 exemplars with crisp, feature-based reasons.
Failure: model gives generic "A is better because it's more relevant."
Hypothesis: the model latches to surface-level phrase templates when few-shot examples are homogeneous.
Mitigation: diversify exemplars (include failure examples) and add explicit rubric tokens (e.g., "score: {precision}, explanation: 1-sentence focusing on feature mismatch").

3) Multi-step extraction -> partial outputs (misses last entity)
Pattern: when prompt sets ask for enumerated entities, models truncate last item or merge two items.
Potential cause: token budget + ambiguous separators.
Mitigation experiments: enforce numbered output, add trailing guard token ("END_OF_LIST"), increase temperature=0.0 for determinism.
Result so far: guard token + numbered list recovered last item in 7/10 runs.

Variant assembly heuristics (working list):
- Anchor the last line: always end with explicit output marker ("Return only JSON array: ...").
- When examples are near-identical, intentionally perturb one exemplar's phrasing to avoid mimicry.
- If hallucination is UI-specific, include 1 negative exemplar that explicitly says "Do not invent UI paths."
- For fairness-sensitive tasks, include a reasoned rubric in the cue-template.
- When the model tends to repeat the prompt header in the answer, shift the header to a system-like instruction (try prompting via role insertion rather than inline preface).

Experiment matrix (sketch):
Columns: [cue-type (concise | role-expanded), exemplar-count (1/2/4/6), exemplar-order (chronological | shuffled | hardest-first), scaffold (none | stepwise), negative-ex (0|1), output-guard (none | marker | JSON schema)]
Rows: prioritized by customer impact (CS tickets) + internal kpis (accuracy of extraction / hallucination rate).

Logging & triage tags I add when a run fails:
- FAIL_TYPE: hallucination | truncation | repetition | formatting | wrong-granularity
- SEVERITY: low | medium | high (high if customer-facing generation or PII risk)
- NOTE: quick repro prompt + model + params + short curl snippet

Sample log entry: 
- FAIL_TYPE: truncation
- SEVERITY: medium
- MODEL: open-model-v2-16k
- PROMPT: (see minimal repro 3)
- PARAMS: temperature=0.0, max_tokens=128
- NOTES: last entity omitted ~30% of runs; guard token recovered in majority. Link -> JIRA:PRJ-2217

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Does adding a single tiny negative exemplar help equally across model sizes (125M -> 7B -> 16B)? Need cross-size sweep.
- Can we automatically detect risk of UI-hallucination by scanning customer examples for UI-nouns ("click, menu, page") and auto-insert a negative exemplar?
- Explore ordering heuristics: is hardest-first ordering better for classification-like outputs?

Quick reproducible prompts to stash for CI tests (short):
- "Convert below customer message into tone: professional, 1-sentence summary:" + 2 examples + input. Target checks: length <= 24 words, no speculative language.
- "Extract all entity:value pairs; return JSON array. Do not invent keys." + 3 examples. Target checks: JSON parseable, keys match allowed set.

Random musings (notes to self):
- Keep the library small: 40–80 canonical variants per use-case. We were getting noise when we tried combinatorial explosion.
- Consider a light-weight metadata layer: variant -> observed fail tags -> quick mitigation suggestion. That can live as CSV for now.
- For user-copyable templates, bake in a one-line 'safety' line: e.g., 'Do not add UI steps; if uncertain, respond "Refer to docs."'.

References and quick links:
- GH prototype with generator + sample corpus: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-tools/pull/237
- Current CS triage: JIRA PRJ-2217 (screenshot attachments of failing outputs)
- Slack thread with field reports: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0PROMPT/p1678901234000

If I come back later: baseline experiments to record immediately -> exact prompt text, 5 seeds (different random seeds), and a binary pass/fail for each check (formatting, hallucination, completeness). Save as CSV row.

End of scratchpad (for now).
